blocks.text: `docker run` = pull if missing + create + start (+ attach unless -d). Options before the image name configure the container; everything after it replaces CMD.

$ docker run -d --name api --network rag_net -p 127.0.0.1:8000:8000 \
    --env-file .env -v hf_cache:/models --memory 2g --cpus 1.5 \
    --restart unless-stopped --init --read-only --tmpfs /tmp --user 10001:10001 \
    ghcr.io/acme/rag-api:1.4.2

rows: Must be unique; also a DNS name on user-defined networks
Binds 0.0.0.0 unless you prefix an IP
Fixed at creation; changes need a new container
Silently creates missing host paths as root-owned dirs
Default bridge has no container DNS
Only the executable; args go after the image
Apps writing to cwd/$HOME break; add --tmpfs
Default is `missing`: stale local tags are used silently

blocks.text: `docker run myimage --rm` passes `--rm` to the app, not to Docker. Order is semantic.

Q: "What does docker run actually do?" A: "It pulls the image if it's missing, creates a container (writable layer, config, mounts, network endpoint), starts it, and attaches to its output unless -d is set. Options before the image configure the container; arguments after it replace CMD."

items: Docker flags go before the image name.
Env, mounts and ports are fixed at creation.
Default pull policy reuses stale local tags.
